name: Spilno.us
description: Ukrainian professional services directory for the Texas community — a React SPA on Vercel that reads approved listings through serverless functions, accepts public submissions reviewed via a Telegram bot or an admin dashboard, and stores data in Supabase Postgres.

nodes.label: Public user
nodes.detail: Browses the directory and submits listings

nodes.label: Admin / reviewer
nodes.detail: Approves & deletes via dashboard or Telegram taps

nodes.label: POST /api/delete-image
nodes.detail: Deletes one Cloudinary image by public id (requires Supabase Bearer token)

nodes.label: keep-alive cron
nodes.detail: Vercel Cron 0 0 * * *, CRON_SECRET-gated — pings DB to keep it warm; alerts Telegram on failure, pings healthchecks.io on success

nodes.label: cleanup-images cron
nodes.detail: Vercel Cron 0 3 * * 0, CRON_SECRET-gated — deletes orphaned Cloudinary images (48h grace period) AND backs up the services table to GitHub

nodes.label: services table
nodes.detail: Supabase Postgres, RLS: public reads approved=true

nodes.label: Cloudinary
nodes.detail: Image hosting — unsigned upload + signed admin delete

nodes.label: GitHub
nodes.detail: Contents API — commits a weekly services.json backup to the data-backups branch

nodes.label: healthchecks.io
nodes.detail: Dead-man's-switch — keep-alive pings it on success; alerts if a ping is ever missed

flows.name: Submit a listing
flows.description: Public user adds a business: images upload straight to Cloudinary, then the form posts to the API which validates, rate-limits, inserts an unapproved row, and pings Telegram.

flows.name: Browse the directory
flows.description: Visitor loads the homepage; the SPA reads approved listings through the serverless API, never touching Supabase directly.

steps.label: Opens the directory
steps.detail: search & category filter live in HomePage state

flows.name: Approve from Telegram
flows.description: Reviewer taps Approve in the Telegram message; the webhook verifies the secret, flips approved=true, and edits the message.

steps.label: Set approved=true
steps.detail: update().eq('id', uuid) — idempotent if already approved

flows.name: Delete from Telegram
flows.description: Reviewer taps Delete; the webhook removes the listing's Cloudinary images, then the row, then edits the message.

flows.name: Admin signs in
flows.description: Admin authenticates against Supabase Auth from the browser; the resulting session unlocks RLS-gated full access.

steps.label: Session token
steps.detail: authenticated session enables admin RLS policy

flows.name: Manage queue (dashboard)
flows.description: Authenticated dashboard reads pending rows directly via supabase-js; deleting calls the image API (with Bearer token) then removes the row.

steps.label: Read / update / delete
steps.detail: supabase-js direct, anon key + admin RLS (approved=false rows)

flows.name: Keep-alive cron
flows.description: A daily Vercel Cron invocation runs a trivial query so Supabase doesn't idle out. Registered in vercel.json's "crons" array and gated behind a CRON_SECRET bearer-token check — both were missing until 2026-09-14, which is why this cron had silently never run and Supabase auto-paused (see docs/db-pause-recovery-plan.md).

steps.label: SELECT id LIMIT 1
steps.detail: vercel.json "crons" schedule 0 0 * * *; 401s without Authorization: Bearer $CRON_SECRET; throws on supabase-js { error } instead of swallowing it

steps.label: Ping on success
steps.detail: Dead-man's-switch — no-op until HEALTHCHECK_URL is set

steps.label: Alert on failure
steps.detail: sendTelegramAlert(...) only when the DB ping throws

flows.name: Orphan image cleanup + services backup
flows.description: Weekly cron does two independent jobs on the same schedule (Vercel Hobby caps a project at 2 cron jobs, both already used by this and keep-alive): lists all Cloudinary images, cross-references against the services table, and deletes orphans older than 48 hours; separately, backs up the full services table to GitHub. CRON_SECRET-gated — this endpoint had no auth at all until 2026-09-14 and was a live, exploitable public deletion trigger (see docs/security-audit.md, Finding 10).

steps.label: Fetch full table (backup)
steps.detail: select * — independent try/catch from the cleanup logic below; runs first

steps.label: Commit JSON snapshot
steps.detail: backupServicesToGitHub() — creates the data-backups branch if missing, overwrites backups/services.json each run

steps.label: Fetch all image URLs
steps.detail: select images from services — aborts on query error or null data

steps.label: Delete orphaned images
steps.detail: Skip images < 48h old; delete those not referenced by any service

steps.label: Send alert
steps.detail: Reports count deleted/failed for cleanup, and separately for a backup failure — neither masks the other

meta.notes: Server _lib helpers (api/_lib/supabase.js, telegram.js, cloudinary.js, github.js) are folded into the functions that call them. 'services-table' represents the Supabase Postgres `services` table; 'supabase-auth' is the same Supabase project's Auth service, split out so the admin-login flow reads clearly. Public reads go only through /api/services; the admin dashboard talks to Supabase directly with the anon key under RLS. The local Vite dev middleware reimplements /api/submit-service with looser validation — this map reflects the authoritative deployed api/*.js handlers. Both crons were fixed 2026-09-14: they'd never actually run (dead config.schedule export, ignored by Vercel) and cleanup-images had no auth at all — see docs/db-pause-recovery-plan.md and docs/security-audit.md (Findings 10/10a).
